Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB298.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shenfeng Xian. Shenfeng Xian owns the retained address: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — then, suddenly raising the whisk: may this be called the ground? Striking the seat: may this be called the teaching? Letting the whisk fall: muddle on, then, if you must — but hesitate, and you are a thousand, ten thousand miles away. If it goes so, this mountain monk is all of you, and you are not him; if not, you are him, and he is not you. A long silence — go back to the hall and drink tea.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB233.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jie'an Jin. Jie'an Jin owns the retained small-meeting: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born. Since Wujin came to dwell at Jinming he has kept the door shut six years, sick through the seasons — and now the officers press a sick monk to close the retreat: not one stick of wood, not one grain of rice, not one stalk of greens, utterly empty — so that roaming monks who arrive and see it earn a share of split lips laughing. Tonight it cannot be helped; an old case is raised: of old Muzhou egging Linji on to ask his question — not a kind heart; Yangqi asking Ciming to the evening meeting — not a kind heart. Tonight the officers press this sick monk to close the retreat — kind heart, or not? Try to settle it.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB235.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lianyue. Lianyue Daozheng owns the retained address: he raised the whisk — the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — then drew a circle with it: true awakening has no name or form; follow the conditions, and there is the seat of the way. From the founders on, all have built their gates inside this one seat, each setting out his own device — the flower raised, the wall faced, the tablet danced, the ball bowled — no two holdings alike. This mountain monk today will not go circling outside either; he runs one straight rule, bent only on making all of you see a resting place on the spot — only, do not catch at echoes. The whisk flung down, one shout: a thousand skills all spring rain — one shout like thunder wakes the hibernating dragon.

Huijue Yi owns the retained small-meeting: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — but if the ground is not there at all, from where would the teaching stand? The dried turd-stub, three pounds of hemp, the Chenzhou radish-head, the cypress tree in the yard — what then of these? He rapped the staff: strung through, all on one string.

Senses.Explanation: The teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — the couplet that opens an occasion and then gets its footing pulled. Shenfeng Xian, opening the hall: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — and suddenly the whisk: may this be called the ground? the seat struck: may this be called the teaching? the whisk dropped: muddle on if you must, but hesitate and you are a thousand, ten thousand miles away — if it goes so, this mountain monk is all of you and you are not him; a long silence — go back to the hall and drink tea. Zhangxue Tongzui, pulling the couplet's footing: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — but if the ground is not there at all, from where would the teaching stand? the whisk raised — this is the ground, what is the teaching? — flung down: thrown on the sweepings-heap, for the rain to beat and the wind to blow away. Jie'an Jin, at the small-meeting: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — since Wujin came to Jinming, door shut six years, sick through the seasons, and now the officers press a sick monk to close the retreat: no wood, no rice, no greens, utterly empty — the roaming monks split their lips laughing; an old case is raised — Muzhou egging Linji on, not a kind heart; Yangqi asking Ciming to the evening meeting, not a kind heart — tonight's pressing, kind heart or not? try to settle it. Lianyue Daozheng, at the restored monastery: whisk raised — the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — a circle drawn in the air: true awakening has no name or form; follow the conditions, and there is the seat of the way; the founders all built their gates inside this one seat — flower raised, wall faced, tablet danced, ball bowled — this mountain monk runs one straight rule: see a resting place on the spot, only do not catch at echoes; the whisk flung down, one shout: a thousand skills all spring rain, one shout like thunder wakes the hibernating dragon. Huijue Yi, for the layman of Pingshan: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — if the ground is not there, from where would the teaching stand? the turd-stub, three pounds of hemp, the radish-head, the cypress tree — what of these? the staff rapped: strung through, all on one string. Wenmu Nian, opening the hall: the teaching never rises alone; it takes a ground to be born — the staff raised, the assembly called: is this the teaching, or the ground? settle it, and it is seventy-three eighty-four with you; failing that — we meet on another peak.
